text:
emily: quick thought from today's spike — what if we publish two independent checksums in manifests: a download-level hash (cipher_hash) and a logical-model hash (model_hash). registry can route fetches by cipher_hash to avoid duplicate transfers when mirrors keep identical ciphertext.

tom: sounds useful. how do we compute model_hash when publishers encrypt differently per-region?

emily: publisher tooling should compute model_hash over canonicalized weights before encryption. cipher_hash is computed after encryption. manifest carries both, plus per-chunk checksums for streaming verify.

maria: important: we need canonicalization rules for model_hash: deterministic ordering of metadata, strip non-deterministic headers, float serialization precision. otherwise hashes diverge. add an RFC appendix with exact algorithm.

emily: agreed. also plan for two fetch paths:
- fetch_by_cipher(cipher_hash): registry returns an origin that has that exact ciphertext blob
- fetch_by_model(model_hash): registry returns origin + a flag indicating ciphertext may differ; loader will request and verify after decrypt

tom: streaming verify tradeoffs: verifying cipher_hash can be done incrementally as bytes stream in. verifying model_hash requires decrypting first (so either buffer or stream-decrypt into verifier). buffering costs RAM and latency.
maria: can we stream-decrypt into verifier without storing plaintext to disk? yes, but we must ensure decryption key is available early and that integrity tag is validated last for AE schemes. streaming-decrypt-then-verify will still need to hold a window if AE tag is at end.
emily: practical compromise: prefer cipher_hash dedupe by default. only fall back to model_hash verification when cipher hashes differ or when registry only knows model_hash.
tom: operationally, who computes those? packager service writes both hashes; if packager can't access plaintext (customer-supplied keys) it only writes cipher_hash. registry needs to persist both fields but only for new publishes. backfill not required.
maria: metrics: add counters: dedupe_hit, dedupe_miss, verify_fail, origin_switch_count, streamed_bytes_saved. set alert if verify_fail_rate > 0.2% for a model or if origin_switch_count spikes.
emily: rollout suggestion:
1) manifest additive fields, loader ignores unknown fields
2) registry stores cipher_hash for new publishes, packager emits both when possible
3) canary loaders enable fetch_by_cipher and streaming-cipher-verify
4) after mirror hygiene (ensuring identical ciphertexts) we enable widespread dedupe

tom: testcases: cipher_dedupe_success, cipher_mismatch_then_model_verify_success, decrypt_fail_alert, multi-origin-fallback-on-corrupt-mirror. also stress test low-memory loaders to ensure stream-abort frees buffers.
maria: small API sketch for registry:
```
GET /v1/shards?model=foo -> returns [{"shard_id": "s0", "cipher_hash": "0x..", "model_hash": "0x..", "origins": [...]}]
POST /v1/fetch-by-cipher -> {"cipher_hash":"0x.."} -> 302 to chosen origin
```

emily: infra-bot filed INF-9999 for manifest-v2 + registry fields.

infra-bot: INF-9999 created and linked to RFC-400.

emily: owners: emily (manifest schema + tests), tom (loader streaming verify + buffer handling), maria (canonicalization doc + registry contract). i'll draft short RFC follow-up and copy these snippets.

tom: +1. i'll prototype streaming-cipher-verify helper and a small cli to compute chunked cipher_hash.
maria: +1. i'll write canonicalization appendix and a sample implementation in python.
emily: one last thought: chunk-level dedupe across shards is interesting but out-of-scope for initial rollout. logging it as future-epic.

emily: closing thread; RFC stub incoming. thanks all :rocket:
